action: opened the order: Invent one new widget that goes beyond everything in the catalog. One remarkable idea, or none.
Untapped capability: proposed This (point-widget, ui.selection as a referent for the next prompt), Easel (easel-widget, real pixels through the Image element)
person-at-the-terminal lens: proposed Peek (peek-widget), Strays (strays-widget), Gloss (gloss-widget)

Delight: proposed Unsent (unsent-widget, what you typed and deleted before sending, from prompt.edit), Narrator (narrator-widget, a nature documentary about the session, model.complete + audio.speak), Second Thoughts (doubletake-widget, the moments Claude changed its mind, from turn.step thinking chunks)
took the order at ideation

stamped reject on "This": A variation on Margin (WO-0016, already on the floor), which also takes the mouse selection and turns it into a prompt; attaching it silently on a pointing word adds little beyond that and risks sending text unasked.
stamped reject on "Peek": The same widget as Loupe (WO-0020, already on the floor): select a word, see its definition, path or commit, with no model.

stamped reject on "Easel": Image paints pixels only in kitty and Ghostty, so on this machine and most terminals it is a file-name card, and neither the inspector nor the demo page can see the thing that makes it remarkable.

stamped reject on "Gloss": A variation on stakes in the same slot under the permission dialog, resting on parsing ten tools' help text, which differs per tool and on Windows is missing (no man; git --help opens a browser).

stamped reject on "Unsent": A variation on mirror (a portrait of how you talk to Claude) whose novelty wears off after a day, and the one useful part, restoring a lost draft, the prompt box's own undo already covers.
stamped reject on "Narrator": A variation on dream, postcard and fortune (a model-written quip about the session) that costs a model call every turn, and its speech works on macOS only.
stamped reject on "Second Thoughts": It rests on thinking text arriving whole, which the inventor could not confirm, and a fixed phrase list over summarised thinking gives a count nobody can trust.
named the widget strays-widget ("Strays")

stamped pass: Strays is the only idea that neither repeats a widget on the floor nor rests on something this machine cannot show: it answers a pain everyone has met (a port still held by a server Claude left running), with no tokens and API that already exists.

Finding 1, what the facts script printed (real, from inside a Claude Code session on this machine, for a bun server a Bash call with run_in_background left on 47614; no claude session was run by the machinist, so it was asked from the PowerShell tool, not from $.process.run): self 11916 <- cmd.exe 2548 <- claude.exe 8604; listener bun.exe 3920 (born +2.3 s) <- bash.exe 12364 (+1.7 s) <- bash.exe 6952 (+0.3 s) <- bash.exe 9676 <- claude.exe 8604 <- powershell.exe 5784 <- WindowsTerminal.exe 10944. Read with the old rule (host = parent of self) host is cmd.exe 2548, the chain climbs past claude.exe to the terminal and the row is refused: cause (b) is real wherever PowerShell is reached through a shell. Fixed: host is the first process above self that is not cmd, powershell or pwsh; the script now prints self's own parents too. Cause (a) is also real: stop ran its own listing and facts call beside the refresh already running, two PowerShells at once at 100% CPU. Whether $.process.run itself goes through a wrapper is still unverified (its doc says argv, no shell); the next live run decides, and stop now says so if it could not look.

Findings 2, 3, 5: stop goes through refresh (waits for the one in flight and exactly one queued after it; never a second listing or facts call beside it; the promise in flight is held in a module-level const Map because a promise cannot live in $.state); with no row and a fault it answers 'Could not check port N: cannot read processes.' or '...: cannot list ports: netstat failed.'; A2 feeds the captured output above unedited (LIVE_FACTS) and replays the live script: row ':47614 bun', 'Stopped bun on :47614 (pid 3920).', then 'Nothing of this session's is on port 47614.'; A5 proves the queue, A12 the fault answers. Checker passes, 20 tests.

Finding 4, measured (4 cores at 100%, three rounds each, spawned by argv from bun): bare 'powershell -NoProfile -NonInteractive -Command 1' 7.3 to 7.8 s; cmd /c ver 1.6 s; netstat 1.6 s; the facts call with the slim table only 11.4 to 12.8 s; with the command line of the one hinted listener read by key (new) 11.4 to 12.4 s; the old two-query script 12.5 to 15.4 s. Tried and slower: [wmisearcher] 16 to 26 s, WbemScripting COM 19 to 27 s. The command line now costs under 0.5 s and is asked only for listeners named node, bun, python and the like, never for stop's born check. What is left is PowerShell starting (half the bound) and the CIM module loading (about 4 s); neither can be cut while the spec's argv is powershell -Command, so the margin at full load is about 3 s, not 'well under'. The load is not the factory's work: twelve find.exe processes started between 16:52 and 19:32 today each hold 40 to 90 minutes of CPU (pids 8120 11164 11668 8548 13088 11012 4200 11764 11732 9968 3164 2000); not the machinist's to kill. No idle figure could be taken. If the bar is a busy machine, design must raise the facts timeout or drop PowerShell.

Left running: the throwaway bun server on port 47614 (pid 3920, started from the machinist's Bash tool as a background task for the capture). The taskkill was refused by the permission classifier, so it was not stopped; it should end with the machinist's session. Port 47613 is free. Check 47614 before the next live run.

Correction to the figures above: '12.5 to 15.4 s' is the two-query form (slim table, then one WHERE query for the command lines) rewritten with the new climb, not the shipped old script, which the first build measured at 12.3 s.

stamped send-back to design: The live run failed again: both stops got no answer from the command hook. The spec makes stop await a refresh that another hook started, one at a time; that wait is charged to the engine's 10 s hook budget (HookBudget) while the Windows facts call takes 11 to 12 s, so the hook is dropped. The spec must say what stop does while a refresh is in flight without waiting on it, name a supported way for a refresh to outlive its dispatch (clock.after or session.start, not a bare un-awaited call), raise the facts timeout above 15 s, and make the Live section show a row before stop. Six findings in inspection.md.
